hyps.why: A skip on the direct 0->3 edge already provides a gradient and identity path, so a conv on edge 5 is partly redundant.
The skip on edge 3 makes the extra conv path into node 3 less valuable.
Replacing none with a conv adds a whole new path to the output, whereas replacing skip_connect only swaps one path for another.
A conv after a pooling edge on the serial chain operates on already-blurred, low-resolution features, so it gains less than after a conv.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 receives nothing, so a conv on edge 4 has no signal to process.
Stacked pooling on the 0->1->3 chain over-smooths and loses detail, which hurts most at low resolution on ImageNet16-120.
A second identity path into node 3 duplicates the existing one and adds little.
Convs on both incoming edges of node 2 produce complementary summed features rather than redundant ones.
With edge 1 removed, node 2 is fed only through edge 2, which is reduced by upstream gating, so a conv on edge 5 gains less.
Two convs summed at node 3 compete for the same capacity, so the second adds less than the first.
